title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed page, numbered '4 - 41 -' and 'n° 392', of a Bourbaki draft of Algèbre commutative, Chap. VII (Diviseurs), §4, on finitely generated modules over Dedekind domains. Its blank verso was evidently reused for the manuscript notes on L-functions that make up the surrounding pages. Those pages compute in the Grothendieck group of l-adic sheaves on a curve: E_η^♮ = i_!(E_U) + Σ j_{x*}(E^{I(x)}) and its dual D(E^♮).

The setting is a Dedekind domain A with fraction field K and set P of nonzero primes, and a finitely generated torsion-free (hence projective) A-module M of rank n ≥ 2. The page finishes a lemma: given y ∈ M (with Y the finite set of p where y(p) = 0 in M(p) = M ⊗ k(p)), there is x ∈ M with x(p) ≠ 0 for every p ∈ P. By 'lemma 7 with m = 1', Ax is then a direct summand with projective quotient.

Proof as written:
(i) Let S = A minus the union of the p in Y. Then S^{-1}A is a semi-local principal ring with maximal ideals pS^{-1}A, and S^{-1}M / pS^{-1}M = M(p). By a prime-avoidance or Chinese-remainder statement for semi-local rings (Chap. II, §1, n° 2, prop. 6), some z/s has nonzero image in every M(p), p ∈ Y. Hence z(p) ≠ 0 for p ∈ Y.
(ii) One may assume y and z are K-linearly independent. Otherwise replace z by z + at, with t independent of y and 0 ≠ a in the intersection of the p ∈ Y.
(iii) The set Z of p ∉ Y where y(p) and z(p) become dependent is finite (lemma 7). For p ∈ Z write z(p) = λ(p) y(p).
(iv) By lemma 6 (CRT) choose b ∈ A whose residue differs from λ(p) for every p ∈ Z. Then x = z − by satisfies x(p) ≠ 0 at every p, checked case by case on Y, on Z, and on P − (Y ∪ Z).
The page then begins the induction on n for Theorem 6: M ≅ A^{n−1} ⊕ 𝔞, the Steinitz-type structure theorem.
errors: No mathematical errors. The hypothesis Card(A/p) ≥ 2 is automatic and stronger than needed: the CRT always gives b avoiding one residue at finitely many maximal ideals.
Implicit facts used: Y is the finite set where y(p) = 0; k(p) = A/p because nonzero primes are maximal; s ∈ S is a unit mod p, so z/s ≠ 0 in M(p) implies z(p) ≠ 0. All are fine.

ideas.what: Existence of a unimodular element (nowhere-vanishing fibre value) in a projective module of rank ≥ 2 over a Dedekind domain, via semi-localization and CRT
ideas.modern_name: Unimodular element / Serre's splitting for Dedekind domains; Steinitz structure theorem M ≅ A^{n−1} ⊕ 𝔞
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steinitz (1911–12); Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative Ch. VII §4
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative, Chap. VII, §4 (1965); this is a Bourbaki draft, not Grothendieck's text

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki draft page (Algèbre commutative VII, Dedekind modules) used as scrap paper behind Grothendieck's L-function notes. The content is classical and appears in the published Bourbaki. Nothing new is attributable to Grothendieck here.
transcription_corrections: The page is typewritten (a Bourbaki rédaction, n° 392), not manuscript, and is unrelated to the neighbouring handwritten pages on l-adic sheaves.
The first line continues a sentence from the previous typed page, presumably '... S^{-1}A est un anneau principal semi-local ...'.
The underlined letters p are Fraktur 𝔭 (typewriter convention); the transcription rendering as \mathfrak{p} is correct.
